イギリス領中央アフリカ

states.label: Nyasaland
states.question: Is the country called {name}?
states.cue: Nyasaland (Njassaland, Nyassaland), named after Lake Nyasa.

states.label: Malawi
states.question: Is the country called {name}?
states.cue: Independent Malawi.

transitions.funFact: Britain's protectorate along Lake Nyasa was first called British Central Africa. In 1907 it took the lake's name instead and became Nyasaland. Nyasa simply means "lake" in local languages, so the colony was, in effect, called Lakeland.

Nyasaland became independent on 6 July 1964 as Malawi, a name Hastings Banda took from the Maravi kingdom that ruled the region centuries earlier. The lake became Lake Malawi on the country's own maps, though Tanzania and Mozambique still call their shores Lake Nyasa.

features.title: British Malaya and Borneo, Malaya, or Malaysia
features.subject: Malaya and Borneo

states.label: All British
states.question: Are Malaya and northern Borneo all British territories?
states.claim: Malaya and North Borneo are British
states.cue: The Malay Peninsula (Malaya) and Sarawak and North Borneo along Borneo's north coast are all in Britain's colour, with Singapore at the southern tip.

states.label: Malaya independent
states.question: Is Malaya independent while Sarawak and North Borneo are still British?
states.cue: Malaya has its own colour; Sarawak, North Borneo, Brunei and Singapore are still Britain's.

states.label: Malaysia
states.question: Do the Malay Peninsula and northern Borneo form one country, Malaysia?
states.cue: One colour on both sides of the South China Sea, labelled Malaysia. Only tiny Brunei stays out; Singapore was part of it from 1963 to 1965.

transitions.funFact: The Federation of Malaya became independent on 31 August 1957, while British and Commonwealth troops were still fighting a communist insurgency in its jungles, the Malayan Emergency, which lasted until 1960. Malaya's nine sultans take turns as king for five years each, a system Malaysia still uses.

On 16 September 1963 Malaya joined Singapore, Sarawak and North Borneo (renamed Sabah) to form Malaysia, one country split by some 600 km of sea. Indonesia called it a British plot and fought an undeclared war over Borneo. Singapore was expelled two years later, on 9 August 1965.

features.title: French Sudan, Upper Senegal and Niger, or Mali
features.subject: Upper Niger

states.label: French Sudan
states.question: Is the territory called {name}?
states.cue: French Sudan (Soudan français), the first name of France's conquests on the upper Niger.

states.label: Upper Senegal and Niger
states.question: Is the territory called {name}?
states.cue: Haut-Sénégal-Niger (Upper Senegal and Niger), a colony of French West Africa.

ja: 上セネガル・ニジェール
上セネガル・ニジェール

states.label: French Sudan
states.question: Is the territory called {name}?
states.cue: French Sudan again (Soudan français), often written right across the Sahara.

states.label: Mali
states.question: Is the territory called {name}?
states.cue: Independent Mali, capital Bamako.

transitions.funFact: France's conquests on the upper Niger were first called French Sudan, from the Arabic for "land of the black people". Between 1899 and 1904 the colony was carved up and renamed several times, ending up as Upper Senegal and Niger, the name maps used for the next sixteen years.

In the early 1920s France reorganised West Africa again, and Upper Senegal and Niger got back its old name, French Sudan. Timbuktu, Gao and the inland Niger delta all lay inside it, and for almost forty years maps printed Soudan français across the western Sahara.

French Sudan and Senegal became independent together as the Mali Federation in June 1960, but it broke up after two months. On 22 September the former French Sudan declared itself the Republic of Mali, after the medieval empire of Mansa Musa, often called the richest man who ever lived.

features.title: Manchuria: part of China, or the Japanese puppet state Manchukuo
features.subject: North-east China

states.label: Part of China
states.question: Is Manchuria part of China?
states.cue: China's colour runs north to the Amur; Manchuria is at most a region name, with Mukden (Shenyang) and Harbin as Chinese cities.

states.label: Manchukuo
states.question: Is Manchuria a separate country, Manchukuo?
states.cue: Manchukuo is drawn as its own state from the Amur down to the Great Wall, often in Japan's colour, with the capital Hsinking (Changchun). Maps of 1932 to 1945.

depictions.label: Manchukuo as a country
depictions.question: Is Manchuria a separate country, Manchukuo?
depictions.cue: Its own name and border; most atlases of the time printed Manchukuo, even where their governments did not recognise it.

depictions.label: Still drawn as China
depictions.question: Is Manchuria part of China?
depictions.cue: Some maps ignored the puppet state, following the League of Nations, and kept Manchuria in China's colour.

states.label: Part of China
states.question: Is Manchuria part of China?
states.cue: China's colour runs north to the Amur again; Changchun has its old name back.

transitions.funFact: After blowing up a stretch of its own railway near Mukden in 1931 and blaming China, Japan's Kwantung Army occupied Manchuria and set up Manchukuo with China's last emperor, Puyi, as its figurehead. Changchun became the capital as Hsinking, "new capital". Japan recognised it in September 1932; most of the world never did.

Manchukuo collapsed in ten days when the Soviet Union invaded on 9 August 1945. Puyi abdicated on 17 August and was captured by the Red Army. He spent fourteen years in Soviet and Chinese prisons as a war criminal, and after his release in 1959 worked for a while as a gardener in Beijing.

features.title: Lourenço Marques or Maputo
features.subject: Capital on Delagoa Bay

states.label: Lourenço Marques
states.question: Is the city called {name}?
states.cue: Lourenço Marques (L. Marques).

ja: ロウレンソ・マルケス
ロウレンソ・マルケス

states.label: Maputo
states.question: Is the city called {name}?
states.cue: Maputo, since 1976.

transitions.funFact: The capital of Mozambique was named after Lourenço Marques, a Portuguese trader who explored the bay in 1544. Months after independence, President Samora Machel told a rally on 3 February 1976 that it would be called Maputo, after the river that flows into the bay.

features.title: Iraq, Syria, Lebanon, Transjordan and Palestine: Ottoman, mandates, or independent
features.subject: Fertile Crescent

states.label: All Ottoman
states.question: Is the whole region Turkish (Ottoman)?
states.cue: One Ottoman colour from Anatolia to the Persian Gulf, with province names like Syria, Mesopotamia or Baghdad.

states.label: All mandates
states.question: Are all five lands British or French mandates?
states.cue: Iraq, Transjordan and Palestine marked (Br.) or in British colour; Syria and Lebanon (Fr.) or in French colour.

states.label: Iraq independent
states.question: Is Iraq independent while Syria, Transjordan and Palestine are still mandates?
states.claim: Iraq is independent, the rest mandates
states.cue: Iraq has its own colour and no (Br.); the four lands to the west are still marked British or French.

states.label: Syria and Lebanon independent
states.question: Are Syria and Lebanon independent, with only Transjordan and Palestine still British?
states.cue: Syria and Lebanon have lost their (Fr.); Transjordan and Palestine are still marked British. Maps of 1944 to 1946.

states.label: Only Palestine British
states.question: Is Palestine the only land here still under British mandate?
states.cue: Transjordan is a kingdom of its own; only Palestine, west of the Jordan, is still marked (Br.). Maps of 1946 to 1948.

states.label: All independent
states.question: Are all of these lands independent, with no mandate left?
states.claim: All the old mandates are independent
states.cue: No (Br.) or (Fr.) anywhere: Israel, Jordan, Syria, Lebanon and Iraq each have their own colour.

transitions.funFact: After the Ottoman defeat, the San Remo conference of April 1920 shared out the Arab provinces as League of Nations mandates: Syria and Lebanon to France, Iraq and Palestine, including Transjordan, to Britain. Their borders were drawn largely by British and French officials.

Iraq became fully independent when it joined the League of Nations on 3 October 1932, well before the other mandates here. Its 1930 treaty let Britain keep air bases near Basra and at Habbaniyah, so British influence stayed long after the mandate label went.

In November 1943 the Free French arrested Lebanon's new government for abolishing the mandate, then had to release it under British pressure on 22 November, now Lebanon's independence day. Syria was recognised from January 1944, but French troops stayed until April 1946.

Transjordan became independent on 25 May 1946, when its parliament made Emir Abdullah a king. The British mandate formally ended with the exchange of ratifications that June, leaving Palestine as the last mandate in the region.

Britain gave up the Palestine mandate in May 1948. Israel declared independence the same day and war followed; by 1950 the West Bank was part of Jordan and Gaza was under Egypt, and the word Palestine vanished from most maps.

features.title: Outer Mongolia: part of China, or a country of its own
features.subject: Mongolia

states.label: Part of China
states.question: Is Mongolia part of China, in China's colour?
states.cue: Mongolia is inside China's colour, labelled Mongolia or Outer Mongolia like a province, with no international border along the Gobi.

states.label: Separate, recognised by few
states.question: Is Mongolia part of China, in China's colour?
states.cue: A Soviet-backed People's Republic that China still claimed: Soviet maps draw it as a country, many others keep it inside China.

depictions.label: Country of its own
depictions.question: Is Mongolia a country of its own, outside China's colour?
depictions.claim: Mongolia is a country of its own
depictions.cue: Mongolia has its own colour and an international border with China along the Gobi.

depictions.label: Part of China
depictions.question: Is Mongolia part of China, in China's colour?
depictions.cue: China's claim is respected: Mongolia stays in China's colour.

states.label: Country of its own
states.question: Is Mongolia a country of its own, outside China's colour?
states.claim: Mongolia is a country of its own
states.cue: Mongolia has its own colour and an international border with China along the Gobi.

transitions.funFact: Mongolia broke away when the Qing dynasty fell in 1911, was retaken by Chinese troops in 1919, then seized by a mad White Russian baron, Ungern-Sternberg. In July 1921 Sükhbaatar's partisans and the Red Army took the capital, and Mongolia became the world's second communist state, recognised for decades almost only by the Soviet Union.

China's price for a 1945 treaty with Stalin was a plebiscite: on 20 October 1945 officially every single voter chose independence. The Republic of China recognised Mongolia on 5 January 1946, and from then on almost every map drew it as a country, though Taiwan took the recognition back in 1953.

features.title: Montenegro: own country or part of Yugoslavia
features.subject: Montenegro

states.label: Its own country
states.question: Is Montenegro shown as a country of its own?
states.cue: A border runs round Montenegro and its name is printed like a country's. Before 1918 it was an independent kingdom; since 2006 it is independent again.

states.label: Part of Yugoslavia
states.question: Is Montenegro part of a bigger country together with Serbia?
states.cue: From 1918 to 2006 Montenegro is inside Yugoslavia (from 2003 'Serbia and Montenegro'). The big country's name runs across it; at most a thin republic boundary marks it.

states.label: Independent again
states.question: Is Montenegro a country of its own?
states.cue: Montenegro has been independent since June 2006, with its capital at Podgorica.

transitions.funFact: Montenegro had fought on the winning side in the First World War, yet in November 1918 an assembly in Podgorica deposed its exiled king, Nikola I, and voted to join Serbia. Days later the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes was proclaimed, and Montenegro disappeared from the map for 88 years.

Montenegro's independence referendum on 21 May 2006 needed 55% to pass and got 55.5%, a margin of only about 2,300 votes. Parliament declared independence on 3 June. The country already used the euro, which it had adopted on its own without joining the eurozone.

features.title: Name of India's biggest west-coast city
features.subject: India's great west-coast port

states.label: Bombay

states.cue: Bombay (Bombaim, Бомбей), the name since Portuguese and British times.

states.label: Mumbai
states.question: Is the city called {name}?
states.cue: Mumbai, official since 1995; French, Spanish, Portuguese and Czech maps often keep Bombay.

transitions.funFact: In 1995 the new Shiv Sena-led government of Maharashtra renamed Bombay as Mumbai, after Mumbadevi, the city's patron goddess, saying the old name was a colonial corruption. Bombay had come from the Portuguese Bom Bahia, 'good bay', or from the same goddess; historians still argue.

features.subject: Country west of Thailand

states.cue: Burma (Birma, Birmanie): part of British India until 1937, a British colony until 1948, then independent.

states.cue: Myanmar, the official English name since June 1989; French maps still mostly say Birmanie.

transitions.funFact: A year after crushing pro-democracy protests, the military government changed the country's English name from Burma to Myanmar on 18 June 1989, and Rangoon became Yangon. Both names come from the same Burmese word; for years the opposition, the US and the UK kept saying Burma.

features.title: Name of the desert country on the south-west coast of Africa
features.subject: Desert country in south-west Africa

states.label: German South West Africa

states.cue: German South West Africa, a German colony from 1884.

states.question: Is the country called {name}?
states.cue: South West Africa, a League of Nations mandate run by South Africa from 1920 (in practice from 1915).

states.label: Namibia
states.question: Is the country called {name}?
states.cue: Namibia, independent since March 1990.

transitions.funFact: South African troops conquered German South West Africa in 1915, early in the First World War. In December 1920 the League of Nations gave it to South Africa as a mandate, and the 'German' was dropped from the name, though German place names such as Lüderitz and Swakopmund stayed.

The United Nations renamed the territory Namibia, after the Namib desert, in 1968 and ended South Africa's mandate, but South Africa held on through a 23-year independence war. Namibia finally became independent on 21 March 1990, the last colony in Africa to do so apart from Eritrea's later split.

features.title: Location of Myanmar's capital
features.subject: Myanmar's capital

states.label: Capital inland

states.cue: The star is at Naypyidaw, 320 km north of Yangon; Yangon is shown as an ordinary city.

transitions.funFact: At 6:37 in the morning of 6 November 2005, a time reportedly chosen by astrologers, convoys of lorries began moving Myanmar's ministries from Yangon to a new city cut out of scrubland 320 km to the north. Naypyidaw has motorways up to twenty lanes wide and very little traffic.

features.title: Fort-Lamy or N'Djamena
features.subject: Capital of Chad

states.label: Fort-Lamy
states.question: Is the city called {name}?
states.cue: Fort-Lamy (Ft. Lamy).

states.label: N'Djamena
states.question: Is the city called {name}?
states.cue: N'Djamena, since 1973.

transitions.funFact: Fort-Lamy was named after a French officer, Amédée-François Lamy, killed in 1900 in the battle that won Chad for France. In 1973 President Tombalbaye renamed it N'Djamena, after a nearby Arab village whose name means roughly "place of rest", as part of his campaign for cultural "authenticity".

features.subject: Dutch islands off Venezuela

states.cue: Curaçao, a country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands since 2010.

The new name Netherlands Antilles came with the 1948 revision of the Dutch constitution, and in 1954 the islands became a self-governing country within the Kingdom.

On 10 October 2010 the Netherlands Antilles were dissolved. Curaçao and Sint Maarten became countries within the Kingdom, as Aruba had in 1986, while Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba became special municipalities of the Netherlands itself, using the US dollar.

features.title: Newfoundland and Labrador: a separate dominion, with or without inland Labrador, or part of Canada
features.subject: Newfoundland

states.question: Is Newfoundland separate from Canada, with only a strip of the Labrador coast?
states.claim: Newfoundland has a strip of Labrador
states.cue: Newfoundland has its own colour, and so does a narrow band along the Labrador coast; the interior is Canadian (Quebec) or left vague.

ja: ニューファンドランド

states.question: Is Newfoundland separate from Canada, with a large Labrador reaching far inland?
states.cue: Newfoundland and a big, wedge-shaped Labrador share one colour, separate from Canada; the border runs along the watershed far inland.

states.question: Are Newfoundland and Labrador part of Canada?
states.cue: Newfoundland and Labrador share Canada's colour, with only a thin provincial line.
